common_name: Oaxacan Green Corn (Mexican Heirloom Flour and Tortilla Corn)

planting.note: Direct sow in blocks of at least 4 rows for wind pollination after the danger of frost has passed; Oaxacan Green is a traditional Mexican heirloom dent-flour corn grown for tortillas, tamales, and pozole.

directions: Sow in blocks of at least four rows for reliable wind pollination, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Oaxacan Green is a tall, traditional Zapotec heirloom corn from the Oaxaca region of Mexico, grown for large ears of pale green kernels that dry to a soft cream-green color and grind into a flour prized for tortillas, tamales, and masa-based dishes with a distinctive sweet, complex corn flavor. It grows notably tall, often exceeding 8 feet, reflecting its origins in traditional milpa polyculture systems where it was often interplanted with beans and squash in a Three Sisters-style planting. Allow ears to dry fully on the stalk before harvesting, then cure further indoors before grinding or storing whole. Isolate from other corn varieties by distance or planting-date offset to keep the strain true from seed saved for replanting.
